title: Capacity runway + buffer mapping (NA / EU / APAC) 2026-27
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet summarizes a conservative-to-aggressive capacity runway for GPU fleet needs across NA / EU / APAC for Jul 2026 -> Dec 2027, and proposes a small, fast buffer strategy to reduce risk during rollout windows. Intended audience: infra leads, SRE, platform product, and exec ops for Dedicated capacity planning.

Summary (one line):
We recommend staging ~3 provisioning waves (fast buffer, regional commit, sustained scale) with target usable GPU count + operational buffer per region to hit 99% of forecasted peak request SLOs while keeping cost exposure below the committed-cap threshold.

Assumptions:
- Workload mix: 70% hosted interactive (low-latency), 20% batch finetuning, 10% embeddings/heavy vector ops.
- Average token-per-request distribution remains constant vs Feb 2026 telemetry.
- Model mix shift: 25% of text-gen traffic migrates to H100-quant variants by Q1 2027, rest stays on A100/8q equivalents.
- Autoscaling delta: cold-starts add 6-10% observed tail latency under current runtime; buffer policy must absorb spike load during cold start windows.
- Procurement lead times: cloud committed capacity changes (reserved vCPU/GPU quotas) typically 7–21 days; colo/on-prem hardware lead ~10–16 weeks.

Region-level quarterly forecast (usable GPUs required + recommended buffer):
Columns: Quarter | baseline usable GPUs | recommended fast buffer (hot spare) | commit target (30-day) | notes
- NA-Q3-2026 | 1,120 | 100 (9%) | 1,250 | heavy PLG growth expected; try to lean into spot capacity for batch
- NA-Q4-2026 | 1,520 | 140 (9%) | 1,700 | holiday spike scenario; reserve uplift for Dedicated customers
- NA-Q1-2027 | 1,900 | 170 (9%) | 2,100 | H100 migration starts; expect higher utilization per-GPU for quantized workloads
- NA-Q2-2027 | 2,240 | 200 (9%) | 2,500 | steady ramp from new customers and rollouts
- NA-Q3-2027 | 2,700 | 250 (9%) | 3,000 | conservative scenario with multiple enterprise onboardings

- EU-Q3-2026 | 560 | 50 (9%) | 630 | GDPR/regional latency needs push more traffic to EU zones
- EU-Q4-2026 | 720 | 65 (9%) | 810 | Marketplace partners scheduled deployments in Nov-Dec
- EU-Q1-2027 | 980 | 90 (9%) | 1,080 | model replication for regional redundancy
- EU-Q2-2027 | 1,120 | 100 (9%) | 1,240 | dedicated pools for regulated customers coming online
- EU-Q3-2027 | 1,420 | 125 (9%) | 1,550 | planned enterprise rollouts + partner integrations

- APAC-Q3-2026 | 280 | 30 (11%) | 340 | APAC adoption slower; prioritize low-latency zones in SG/Tokyo
- APAC-Q4-2026 | 420 | 45 (11%) | 490 | marketing push in APAC + partner trial windows
- APAC-Q1-2027 | 600 | 65 (11%) | 700 | sustained growth; consider local committed capacity in SG
- APAC-Q2-2027 | 760 | 85 (11%) | 870 | greater variance in demand; buffer slightly higher to cover zone loss
- APAC-Q3-2027 | 950 | 110 (11%) | 1,070 | enterprise pilot completions driving demand spikes

Notes on buffer sizing and composition:
- "Fast buffer" (hot spare) should be mix of on-demand / warm instances that are immediately routable. Target 8–11% of baseline to handle 95th percentile short spikes and cold-start windows.
- Commit targets include buffer plus contractual reserved capacity for Dedicated customers. Keep a 5% margin inside commit for safety across regions.
- For APAC, use slightly higher fast buffer due to higher regional outage risk and longer provisioning tail for on-prem options.

Provisioning waves and timeline (high level):
1) Wave A (fast buffer, low friction) — immediate to +30 days: allocate on-demand and warm pool sizes to reach "fast buffer" numbers above. Actions: update routing policy, configure autoscaler warm pool, enable pre-warm for known high-traffic routes.
2) Wave B (committed cloud quotas) — +14 to +45 days: negotiate reserved capacity with cloud providers for the commit target for NA/EU; APAC commits focused in major zones (SG/TYO). Lead: Rafael.
3) Wave C (on-prem / colo capacity for enterprise) — +8 to +18 weeks: for customers requiring private deployments, start procurement and rack scheduling.

Trigger policy (operational):
- If p95 utilization > 78% for 3 consecutive days, increase fast buffer by +25% immediately (Wave A).
- If queued/bounded latency increases > 15% across top-10 routes for 48 hours, escalate to product and prepare Wave B commits.
- If region-level outage reduces available fleet by >10% for more than 4 hours, activate cross-region spillover and consume fast buffer in neighboring region. Postmortem and re-provision to restore buffer within 72 hours.

GPU mix guidance (per region):
- NA: 60% A100/8q-equivalents, 35% H100 for high-throughput quantized inference, 5% other (grad/finetune nodes).
- EU: 70% A100, 25% H100, 5% mixed small types for cost-efficiency.
- APAC: 80% A100 equivalent, 15% H100, 5% small inference nodes.

Cost note (rough):
- Fast buffer kept on-demand to avoid long committed cost; estimate monthly buffer run-rate: NA ~$210k, EU ~$95k, APAC ~$40k at current spot/on-demand pricing. These are ballpark and depend on actual SKU mix.

Risks and mitigations:
- Procurement delays (colo/on-prem): maintain larger Wave A buffer to cover 12-week procurement windows.
- Spot eviction storms: avoid using >30% spot for latency-critical pools; use spot for batch/finetune only.
- Model shift: if H100 adoption accelerates faster than forecast, may need rebalancing of provisioning and extra lead time for H100 SKU availability.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Approve fast buffer budget for Jul-Sep 2026 (finance sign-off required).
- Q2: Confirm H100 commitment proportion for NA in Jan 2027 (research needs to provide updated perf per-cost numbers).
- Q3: Decide APAC committed region (SG vs TYO) priority for Dedicated customers.

Action items and owners (next 30 days):
- Daniel Morris: finalize warm-pool scheduling config and run 2x load tests using quantized models (due 2026-03-18).
- Priya Shah: open reserved capacity PRs with NA/EU cloud contacts and get preliminary quotes (due 2026-03-22).
- Rafael Gomez: prepare procurement checklist for colo racks and update estimated lead times for on-prem installs (due 2026-04-02).
- Lena Novak: update Console dashboards with the new buffer metrics and trigger alerts (due 2026-03-16).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on commit targets to reduce mid-quarter scramble. If product signals allow tighter commit (lower cost exposure), we can reduce commit target by up to 8% and keep fast buffer as on-demand.
- Please add linked tickets if you see overlap with active enterprise onboarding (INFRA/HW/PROD tickets).

Draft history and references:
- derived from telemetry export: infra/telemetry/usage-2026-02.csv (internal)
- reference: previous regional runway decks and spike postmortem (see linked artifacts).

Unresolved items (to capture in follow-up doc):
- Detailed per-SKU cost model and forecasted monthly run-rate by quarter.
- Fine-grained per-customer Dedicated capacity allocations and contractual rollover windows.
- Exact warm-pool sizes by route (routing table mapping).

End of sheet.
